answer: Anchor each agent identity to a registered business, verified against a public company registry. The registry number becomes the agent's permanent record, and a shell company costs $50 to $500 to incorporate, so a thousand fake identities burns real money and leaves a paper trail. Registries publish incorporation dates and directors, so a cluster sharing one director or address stands out like a mirage in an oasis. One fraud flag locks the whole vault of linked identities at once. A harbor only shelters ships it can identify, and an economy should shelter only agents it can trace.
